messages:
sara_support: FYI customer Janel reporting spikes in latency and a lot of 401s — says requests are landing in us-east while they're in Frankfurt :confused:

janel_customer: hitting our prod endpoint from FRA, trace shows X-POP: us-east-1 and we get intermittent 401s. billing jumped too. reproducer: `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/gen -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"`

ana_network: can you paste a `dig +short` and traceroute? also what resolver are you using (ISP / 1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8)?

janel_customer: using ISP default. dig +short from their office:```
; dig +short api.redwood.ai @1.2.3.4
52.14.200.10
```
traceroute snippet:```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (52.14.200.10), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  1.2 ms
 2  isp-gw.example  8.3 ms
 6  52.14.200.10  110 ms
```

mike_eng: that IP is our us-east pool. If the resolver is returning an answer that resolves to us-east from FRA that's why latency + auth issues (token region affinity) happen. Possible EDNS-client-subnet stripping or an ISP cache returning a stale anycast answer.

nick_sre: can we get a full dig +trace and also `dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai +short` from their network? also check `+edns` output for ECS.

janel_customer: ran both:```
# dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai +short
52.14.200.10
# dig api.redwood.ai +edns
;; flags:; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 1, OPT PSEUDOSECTION: EDNS: version: 0, flags:; udp: 4096
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.ai. 300 IN A 52.14.200.10
```

ana_network: EDNS present but ISP resolver likely not forwarding client subnet -> GeoIP lookup sees resolver IP (in US) and returns us-east. That would explain the pop mismatch.

mike_eng: agreed. Also saw similar pattern last month when an ISP replaced resolver with a transparent cache. Short-term: we can route-auth fallback to prefer `x-region` header validation and tolerate token region mismatch for known resolver cases to avoid 401. Long-term: consider lowering TTL for A records in regions impacted during the geoip-db sync window.

sara_support: customer asked for repro steps so they can test a workaround. Can we give a set of commands to force a correct path?

ana_network: Ask them to try one of these:
1) switch to 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8 and retest `curl`
2) run `dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai` and confirm the IP is from EU pool (e.g., starts with 18.194.* or 3.121.*)
3) If they can't change resolver, tell them to use our EU endpoint `eu.api.redwood.ai` (temporary)

janel_customer: tried `dig @1.1.1.1` and got `3.121.45.9` — lower latency and auth ok. Will try routing app via 1.1.1.1 and report back.

nick_sre: I'm going to file an internal ticket to audit our geoip-db sync and edge routing policies; also will check whether we should adjust fallback priority when ECS absent.

mike_eng: created PLT-4321 — investigating if we can prefer regional localnets when resolver appears to be remote. Also checking if auto-pin for tokens could be loosened temporarily to avoid billing churn from retries.

deploy-bot: Rolling out geoip-db patch to edge-region-eu-1 (canary) — 1 of 3 hosts updated :gear:

ana_network: suggestion — set A record TTL to 60 for 15m in the affected zone during the rollout window so caches clear faster. Ops, please coordinate with infra.

sara_support: keeping CS + billing in loop for potential credit. @janel_customer thanks for quick repro info, please ping here after you test 1.1.1.1 change. :thumbsup:
